item.title: Beyond the price tag: What Puma the Boer goat can teach us about trust, genetics and the real value of livestock
item.description: The sale of Puma, a Boer goat, for R30 000 didn’t stir much controversy outside of those specifically interested in Boer goat genetics. Although top Boer goat genetics can fetch prices in the six-figure range, the sale of Puma for R30 000 may have been viewed as a subpar deal.

item.title: From our editor: The world is watching – Why unity matters in SA’s FMD fight
item.description: I recently spent part of a morning with a group of French tourists who wanted to visit a farm owned by a black farmer. As African Farming, we were approached by their tour guide to help identify a suitable farm close to Gauteng, allowing the group to remain near other activities on their itinerary.

item.title: Biosecurity, trade disruptions and climate variability defined SA agriculture in 2025
item.description: During the Nedbank Agriculture Webinar on 28 January, Dr Tracy Davids delivered a comprehensive analysis of South African agriculture’s performance in 2025, revealing a sector that successfully navigated from crisis to recovery while confronting new challenges. As executive director of Commodity Markets and Foresight at the Bureau for Food and Agricultural Policy, her insights provided a crucial perspective on the industry’s resilience and emerging concerns.

item.title: FMD | Free State man arrested for refusing inspection
item.description: A Free State man has been arrested after allegedly refusing to grant state officials access to his property to conduct a foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) inspection.

item.title: ‘You are the driver of your own agricultural destiny,’ transformation leader tells farmers
item.description: Scores of farmers recently gathered at the Agricultural Research Council (ARC) in Rooiwal, Pretoria, to learn about transforming their farm waste into biogas. Officials from the ARC outlined several biogas technology options available in South Africa, each suited to different scales and applications.

item.title: Botswana announces prohibitions following suspected FMD cases
item.description: Botswana has announced various prohibitions and other measures following the recent discovery of suspected cases of foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) among livestock in its Masunga District. If this disease is confirmed there, it will put Botswana’s fiercely protected FMD-free status in jeopardy.

item.title: Record average price for Van Hasselt Angoras
item.description: Consistent quality proved to be the deciding factor at the Van Hasselt and guest seller Angora veld ram auction, held at the Willowmore showgrounds on 15 January.

item.title: BVI steps up regional response as FMD outbreak escalates across SADC
item.description: As foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) continues to pose a threat to livestock systems throughout Southern Africa, the Botswana Vaccine Institute (BVI) has announced several measures to support affected countries. The institute is deploying technical expertise and strengthening regional cooperation to contain the outbreak and safeguard the sector.

item.title: Bhambanana Abattoir: Millions spent, years lost and farmers still waiting
item.description: The Bhambanana Red Meat Abattoir in northern Zululand has stood largely unused and deteriorating for close to 14 years, despite many livestock owners in KwaZulu-Natal’s foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) management area having little to no legal means of earning an income from their animals.
